nih.rationale: The study asks a clear question (item 1 Yes), describes the population and setting (item 2 Yes), recruits a clinically relevant ICU population of moderate-to-severe COVID-19 ARDS on mechanical ventilation (item 3 Yes), and gives an explicit, consistently applied protocol for each PEEP strategy (item 6 Yes). Outcomes are objective, device-derived respiratory mechanics and EIT measures recorded at fixed time points with unchanged ventilator settings (item 7 Yes); all 17 enrolled patients complete the protocol and are analysed (item 9 Yes); and appropriate paired non-parametric tests with p values are reported for the within-patient comparisons (item 10 Yes). These strengths keep the rating out of Poor. The rating falls short of Good because of items 5, 4, 8 and 11: the sample is a small convenience series of 17 patients with no size justification (item 5 No; the authors themselves state the number 'preclude[s] any generalization'), it is not reported whether all eligible patients were enrolled or how patients were selected (item 4 NR), outcome assessment was not blinded (item 8 NR), and outcome measures were taken at a single time point under each PEEP rather than repeatedly before and after (item 11 No). These flaws mainly limit generalisability and precision rather than invalidating the within-patient physiological comparisons, so overall quality is Fair.
